extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, respondents in USPTO disciplinary/reciprocal proceedings, OED staff, and counsel handling USPTO discipline
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedures governing imposition of reciprocal discipline by the USPTO based on a state's disciplinary adjudication (37 C.F.R. § 11.24), including the Selling v. Radford exceptions, burden of proof, scope of review, and remedial duties upon suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of reciprocal discipline (Selling standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: State disciplinary adjudication creates a federal-level presumption that imposition of reciprocal discipline is proper; USPTO will generally impose identical discipline unless respondent establishes one of the Selling elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As stated: 'Reciprocal disciplinary proceedings are not in any sense de novo proceedings.' Under Selling v. Radford and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d), the USPTO Director shall consider the record and shall impose the identical public censure, public reprimand, probation, disbarment, suspension, or disciplinary disqualification unless the practitioner demonstrates by clear and convincing evidence, and the USPTO Director finds there is a genuine issue of material fact that one of the enumerated exceptions applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception — Want of due process (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: The practitioner may avoid reciprocal discipline by showing the procedure elsewhere was so lacking in notice or opportunity to be heard as to constitute deprivation of due process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent must prove a genuine issue of material fact on this ground by clear and convincing evidence. USPTO looks to the state record; mere disagreement with findings is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception — Infirmity of proof (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: The practitioner may avoid reciprocal discipline by showing there was such an infirmity of proof establishing the conduct as to give rise to the clear conviction that the Office could not, consistently with its duty, accept the conclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requires the respondent to show, by clear and convincing evidence, that the state proceeding's proof is so deficient that the USPTO cannot accept the state finding as final. Courts treat this standard narrowly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception — Grave injustice (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: The practitioner may avoid reciprocal discipline by showing that imposition of the same discipline by the USPTO would result in a grave injustice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grave-injustice analysis focuses on whether the severity of the punishment 'fits' the misconduct — i.e., whether the state-imposed discipline was within the range of appropriate sanctions. Factors like third-party conduct (e.g., actions of an ex-spouse), post-adjudication consequences, or personal circumstances are generally irrelevant. Mitigating factors considered and stipulated at the state level are not a basis for further reduction in the reciprocal proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception — Arguments regarding public discipline status (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: The practitioner may raise any argument that the practitioner was not publicly censured, publicly reprimanded, placed on probation, disbarred, suspended or disciplinarily disqualified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such arguments are part of the limited set of issues that can be raised to prevent imposition of identical reciprocal discipline; the practitioner still bears the burden to demonstrate a genuine issue of material fact by clear and convincing evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent's burden of proof and standard of persuasion
rubrics_metrics.description: The respondent must demonstrate, by clear and convincing evidence, that there is a genuine issue of material fact as to one of the Selling/§11.24 exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal courts and the USPTO apply a narrow standard — the respondent carries the burden and must present clear and convincing evidence. The Office is not conducting a de novo review to re-litigate the state proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of USPTO review — not de novo; limited to record
rubrics_metrics.description: Reciprocal disciplinary proceedings are not de novo; the USPTO Director reviews the state record and is not sitting as a court of review to discover errors in the state proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations: In re Barach; In re Surrick; In re Zdravkovich. The Director relies on the state adjudication absent a successful showing under § 11.24(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of stipulation/consent to discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent's stipulation or consent to a state-imposed suspension is dispositive in reciprocal discipline proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the practitioner agreed to the state discipline (e.g., consent order imposing a suspension), that fact is highly persuasive and often dispositive against claims of grave injustice or other exceptions. The Office treated the stipulation as dispositive in this matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: What constitutes misconduct warranting suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: Categories of misconduct supporting suspension include knowingly disobeying tribunal obligations, engaging in conduct involving dishonesty/fraud/deceit, violating criminal laws, conduct prejudicial to administration of justice, exposing the profession or courts to reproach, and conduct contrary to justice/ethics/honesty/good morals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order cites specific rule violations and statutes from Michigan: MRPC 3.4(c) (disobeying tribunal obligations); MRPC 8.4(b) (dishonesty/fraud); MCR 9.104 subsections and MCL statutes (e.g., MCL 750.248, 750.249, 750.356, 750.539c, 750.539d) for making/altering/uttering forged public records, larceny, and eavesdropping. Examples in this case: filing a false certificate of marriage, taking privileged material, sewing a recording device into a child's clothing, knowingly giving false testimony, and disobeying court orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grave-injustice evidentiary limits — relevance of mitigating factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Mitigating factors considered in the state proceeding (absence of prior discipline, personal/emotional problems, cooperation) do not automatically justify further reduction of reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office notes that mitigating factors were already considered at the state level and were part of the stipulation; there is no authority to reconsider them a second time to lessen the reciprocal sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedial orders and practitioner duties upon USPTO suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: When suspension is imposed, the Office will order specific remedial actions and practitioner duties pursuant to 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24, 11.58, and 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples from the Order: publish a notice in the Official Gazette (materially consistent text provided); give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 to state disciplinary agencies, courts, and the public; require compliance with duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58; dissociate respondent's name from any Customer Numbers and USPTO verified Electronic System accounts; prohibit applying for or obtaining a USPTO Customer Number or adding name to a Customer Number until reinstated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and publication obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director will publish a notice in the Official Gazette and give notice to disciplinary agencies and courts of the public discipline and reasons for it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order provides the specific form of the 'Notice of Suspension' and directs publication in the Official Gazette and notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59; also points to OED FOIA Reading Room for disciplinary decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to judicial review and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Review of the final decision by the USPTO Director may be had by a petition filed in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia under 35 U.S.C. § 32 within thirty (30) days after the date of the order recording the Director's action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited procedure: 35 U.S.C. § 32 and E.D. Va. Local Civil Rule 83.5. The Order notifies respondent of this remedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imposition of identical discipline unless exception proven
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director shall impose the identical state-imposed discipline (public censure, reprimand, probation, disbarment, suspension, or disciplinary disqualification) unless respondent proves one of the § 11.24(d) exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical effect: absent a successful, narrow showing under the statutory exceptions, reciprocal discipline will mirror the state sanction (e.g., identical term of suspension).
